coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: You're 28 days out and in taper — this is a shakeout day to keep the engine warm without adding fatigue. Hit 4–5 miles easy (Z2, sub-130 bpm based on your recent trend), then 3–4 × 90-second pickups at race-pace effort (threshold/tempo, ~138–142 bpm). Your resting HR is elevated 7.5 bpm above your 30-day average and your recovery score is 46/100 (moderate), which means your system is still clearing load — don't fight it with a hard session. This short, mixed-intensity work preserves neuromuscular sharpness without pushing glycogen depletion or parasympathetic debt into the weekend. Plan the long run for tomorrow when you've had another sleep cycle to recover.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: With 4–5 miles of mostly Z2 work, you don't need intra-workout carbs, but fuel the pickups: aim for 30–40g of carbs (sports drink, gel, or chew) starting at minute 15 and repeat every 30 minutes through the session. Post-run, eat 40–50g carbs + 20–25g protein within 60 minutes to top glycogen and prime recovery ahead of tomorrow's long run. Your sleep efficiency last night was 70%, which is acceptable but not optimal — slightly elevated carb intake today (aim for 7–8g/kg across the day) will support both recovery from this week's volume and tomorrow's alpine vertical work.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your resting HR spike and moderate recovery score indicate incomplete parasympathetic rebound from last week's 31.1 miles. Prioritize sleep tonight: aim for 8+ hours, cool room (< 65°F), and no screens 30 minutes before bed. Post-run, spend 10–15 minutes on lower-body mobility (hip flexors, quads, glutes) and consider a brief ice bath or 10 minutes in cold water if accessible — with 28 days to race and moderate fatigue accumulation, active cooling will accelerate HRV recovery. Tomorrow morning, check resting HR before you start the long run; if it's still above 72 bpm, dial the long run intensity down and focus on steady Z2 volume.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're in the phase where the work is done — from here, the taper is about trusting your fitness while proving to yourself that you can execute race strategy under fatigue. This shakeout with pickups serves double duty: it reminds your legs what race pace feels like on tired muscle, and it reinforces your confidence that you can still snap when it matters. Julian Alps demands alpine movement economy and grit on steep descents; these 90-second accelerations aren't about ego, they're about anchoring the neuromuscular pattern you'll need in week 4 when the vertical gets real. Stay process-focused, not result-focused, over the next four weeks.
